_note: PLACEHOLDER fallacy metadata for Spot the Fallacy. Replace with the generated bank. Each id maps to a display name + a 2-line description used on first-exposure teaching cards.

ad_hominem.name: Ad Hominem
ad_hominem.description: Attacking the person instead of their argument. Whether they're likeable, qualified, or a hypocrite says nothing about whether their point is actually true.

appeal_to_popularity.name: Appeal to Popularity
appeal_to_popularity.description: Claiming something is true or good because lots of people believe it or do it. How many people agree isn't evidence that they're right.

false_dilemma.name: False Dilemma
false_dilemma.description: Presenting only two options when more exist. It forces a choice between two extremes and hides the middle ground.

hasty_generalization.name: Hasty Generalization
hasty_generalization.description: Drawing a broad conclusion from too few or unrepresentative examples. A tiny sample can't speak for the whole group.

appeal_to_authority.name: Appeal to Authority
appeal_to_authority.description: Treating a claim as true just because an authority or celebrity said it — especially when they're famous rather than an expert on the topic.

valid.name: Valid argument
valid.description: The conclusion genuinely follows from the reasons given. Nothing is wrong with the reasoning.

affirming_the_consequent.name: Affirming the Consequent
affirming_the_consequent.description: If P then Q, and Q is true, so P must be true. Invalid — Q could have other causes entirely.

denying_the_antecedent.name: Denying the Antecedent
denying_the_antecedent.description: If P then Q, and P is false, so Q must be false. Invalid — the conditional never said P was the only route to Q.

base_rate_neglect.name: Base Rate Neglect
base_rate_neglect.description: Judging from how typical a case looks while ignoring how common it is to begin with. A very accurate test for a very rare thing still yields mostly false positives.

survivorship_bias.name: Survivorship Bias
survivorship_bias.description: Drawing conclusions from what made it through while the failures are invisible. The sample you can see is not the sample that existed.

regression_to_mean.name: Regression to the Mean
regression_to_mean.description: Crediting an intervention for an improvement that extreme values produce on their own. Outliers drift back toward average with or without treatment.

equivocation.name: Equivocation
equivocation.description: One word carrying two meanings across the argument. Each step reads fine; the conclusion only follows if you let the sense shift.

circular_reasoning.name: Circular Reasoning
circular_reasoning.description: The conclusion smuggled into the premises. The argument is valid but proves nothing, because you must already accept the point to accept the support.

composition_division.name: Composition / Division
composition_division.description: Assuming what's true of the parts is true of the whole, or the reverse. Properties don't always survive that trip.

no_true_scotsman.name: No True Scotsman
no_true_scotsman.description: Redefining the category to shed a counterexample. The claim survives only by becoming unfalsifiable.

texas_sharpshooter.name: Texas Sharpshooter
texas_sharpshooter.description: Drawing the target around the hits after the fact. A pattern picked out of noise once you're free to choose which data counts.

moving_the_goalposts.name: Moving the Goalposts
moving_the_goalposts.description: Demanding new evidence once the original standard is met. The bar shifts precisely as far as it needs to.

confounding.name: Confounding Variable
confounding.description: Reading cause into a correlation that a third factor explains. Both effects share a hidden common source.

gamblers_fallacy.name: Gambler's Fallacy
gamblers_fallacy.description: Expecting independent trials to correct themselves. The coin has no memory of the last ten flips.

middle_ground.name: Middle Ground
middle_ground.description: Treating the midpoint between two claims as automatically correct. Sometimes one side is simply wrong.
